name: South Africa
hook: Three capitals, Mandela, apartheid and the Orange River: the handful of things South Africa clues always test.

facts.label: three capital cities
facts.statement: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Bloemfontein (judicial) and Cape Town (legislative) — the only one that is also a seaport.

facts.label: Nelson Mandela
facts.statement: Nelson Mandela earned a law degree from the University of South Africa in 1942 and, as president in 1996, oversaw a new democratic constitution.

facts.label: the Zulu
facts.statement: The Zulu are South Africa's largest ethnic group; their beadwork carries meaning in color, shape and design, and the word impala comes from their language.

facts.label: the Orange River
facts.statement: The Orange River is South Africa's longest; it rises in Lesotho, forms the Free State's southwestern boundary, and honors a Dutch prince.

facts.label: diamonds
facts.statement: Diamonds built Kimberley's Big Hole, and in 1867 a child's "pretty pebble" turned out to be a 22-carat one.

facts.label: Namibia
facts.statement: Namibia, once a German colony, gained independence from South Africa in 1990 after a 24-year armed struggle.

facts.label: apartheid
facts.statement: Apartheid was the system of white minority rule in South Africa; Jimmy Carter's book compared Israel's treatment of Palestinians to it.
